title: Financing Infrastructure After LGFVs
gist: Teaser only: Gavekal argues China's infrastructure financing model is broken because Beijing, wary after repeated bailouts of LGFV hidden debts, has curtailed off-balance-sheet funding, and infrastructure projects' returns are too low to attract private capital. With infrastructure fixed-asset investment down 7.3% y/y through October and worsening, the government is choosing weaker growth over funding projects entirely with bonds and accepting rising official debt.

insights.claim: China's central government, made wary by repeated bailouts of local government financing vehicles' (LGFVs) hidden debts, has been gradually curtailing the off-balance-sheet financing that local governments used to deliver high infrastructure investment without inflating official debt figures.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The traditional LGFV-driven infrastructure stimulus channel is being deliberately shut, so do not expect it to be reopened as a growth backstop.

insights.so_what: Expect continued drag on Chinese growth from infrastructure rather than a large bond-financed stimulus; position cautiously on China-infrastructure-sensitive assets.
